headline: NovoJuris Legal advises HomeRun on $12 million Series A+ fundraise
sum: HomeRun Retail, a Bengaluru-based quick-commerce platform for construction materials, closed a $12 million Series A+ round led by Nexus Venture Partners, with repeat participation from Sorin Investments, Titan Capital, Sparrow Capital and Consumer Collective by Atrium. The capital funds geographic expansion into Hyderabad and Pune, supply-chain investment, and technology development for the 60-minute delivery model.
implication: Rapid follow-on structure (Series A+ within 6 months of Series A) reflects investor confidence in unit economics driven by high average order value (~₹7,000) in construction logistics-a model-shifting signal that quick-commerce arbitrage extends beyond low-margin grocery to high-margin B2B2C, where speed fixes procurement delays, not customer convenience.
detail: HomeRun, founded in 2024 by Pukhraj Grewal, operates a dark-store-based delivery network for branded construction and interior materials (cement, plywood, electricals, hardware, paints, adhesives, plumbing supplies), targeting contractors and homeowners. The Series A+ follows a $6.6 million Series A (February 2026, led by Sorin) and a ₹9 crore seed (November 2025), bringing total disclosed capital to $19.6 million. The company has completed over 100,000 orders in Bengaluru, claims 8X year-over-year growth, and aims to expand to Hyderabad and Pune by year-end.

structure.novel: Rapid follow-on within 6 months from Series A (compressed fundraising cycle) signals validation of operating metrics (100k+ orders, 8X YoY growth) and signals a market inflection in quick-commerce expansion beyond groceries into B2B2C construction. Lead investor transition (Sorin → Nexus) with round-table structure common in growth-stage VC.

triggers.note: Nexus Venture Partners (US-based global VC) requires RBI/FEMA registration and valuation certification before capital deployment; triggers transfer-pricing documentation if inter-company transactions occur.
Private company equity issuance requires board resolution and shareholder approval; drag-along and anti-dilution terms documented in CCPS deed.
As logistics/delivery-focused startup, HomeRun liable for product liability claims; capital raised funds quality assurance and delivery SLA enforcement to mitigate exposure.
